Formulation  
Acute onset of gastrointestinal symptoms consistent with gastroenteritis likely precipitated by recent food intake (Chinese takeaway). Symptoms include diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, weakness, and reduced appetite, impacting daily functioning and work attendance. No reported mental health issues or significant psychosocial stressors beyond illness-related impairment. Supportive family environment and patient insight provide protective factors.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Acute gastroenteritis  
- Patient Goal(s): Symptom resolution, restore normal bowel function, return to full work capacity  
- Clinical Goal(s): Manage symptoms conservatively, prevent dehydration, monitor for complications or ongoing illness  
- Actions (Patient): Maintain hydration with fluids; use oral rehydration solutions as recommended; take paracetamol as needed for fever/aches; rest and take time off work for 2–3 days; return for follow-up if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days or worsen  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide education on symptom management; recommend oral rehydration therapy (e.g., Dioralyte); advise use of paracetamol for symptomatic relief; recommend time off work and rest; schedule follow-up if no improvement or deterioration occurs; consider stool testing if symptoms persist  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
  Topics Covered: Gastroenteritis explanation, hydration importance, dietary advice, use of oral rehydration salts, paracetamol dosing, work rest recommendations, when to seek further care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent or worsening diarrhea, continued vomiting, blood in stool, high fever, ongoing weakness  
- Coping Strategies: Hydration, rest, light diet, timely medical review if symptoms do not improve or worsen
